Subject: Capacity fingerprint & burst horizon census — EdgeWell pilot

Tom — thanks again for the demo yesterday. As discussed, to size a short pilot and recommend a committed reserved fleet for your chat+summarization workload, we need a concise traffic census from your side. Below is a compact questionnaire — if you can paste values or attach a small sample CSV, we’ll run a quick cost/latency model and return a recommended pilot footprint within 48 hours.

Essential fields (minimal answers ok):
- Peak concurrent user sessions (observed 1-week peak):
- Typical concurrency distribution (e.g., 70% single-turn, 20% multi-turn 2–5, 10% >5 turns):
- Average prompt length (tokens):
- Average assistant response length (tokens):
- Response streaming used? (yes/no)
- Average latency SLO target (p95 generation time in ms):
- % requests with function/tool calls or external lookups:
- KV cache hit-rate (if using session K/V caching):
- Burst multiplier (observed highest QPS / baseline QPS):
- Preferred pilot duration and start window:

If you don’t have exact telemetry, a sample of 24–72 hours in CSV format with timestamp, session_id, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, and status is perfect — I’ve attached an example CSV (edgewell_traffic_sample.csv) you can copy.

Next steps: once we have these numbers, Karthik and I will draft two options: (A) 14-day pilot with 4x burst headroom, (B) 90-day reserved commit recommendation. Marissa will also propose a mutual action plan and a demo-for-ops session.

Thanks — Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com

Hannah — thanks, this is great. Attached is a small export from our staging traffic (24h) and a short answers list below. I’ve redacted PII but kept session ids and token counts. We can follow up with more if you need.

Quick answers:
- Peak concurrent sessions: 820
- Concurrency distribution: 65% single-turn, 25% 2–4 turns, 10% >4 turns
- Avg prompt length: 48 tokens
- Avg assistant response: 210 tokens
- Streaming: yes for web clients (~60%); server-side calls non-streaming
- Latency SLO (p95): 400ms for generation-only
- % with tool calls/lookup: ~12% (search + invoice lookup)
- KV cache hit-rate: ~18% (we’re still rolling caching in prod)
- Burst multiplier observed: 3.4x (peak traffic spikes during marketing blasts)
- Pilot window: ASAP — prefer Sep 13 start, 14-day pilot

Attaching: edgewell_traffic_sample.csv

Also: can Redwood suggest a conservative pilot footprint and an aggressive one (for production commit) so we can budget both? Procurement looped in if we move to a reserved commitment.

—Tom

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@edgewell.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity fingerprint & burst horizon census — EdgeWell pilot

Thanks Tom — very helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions before we run the sizing tool on the CSV:
1) For the streaming fraction, is streaming used for first-token latency (i.e., user-perceived start) only, while full generation happens server-side? Or do clients consume tokens continuously until generation ends?
2) What’s the distribution of model type per request? (e.g., 60% Llama-2-7b, 30% Llama-2-13b, 10% open RAG with 30k context) — if you don’t have exacts, ballpark is fine.
3) Any night/weekend offload windows where committed capacity could be lower?

Tom — if you can answer 1–2 short bullets, we’ll produce: pilot node count + GPU SKU suggestion + estimated p95 latency under continuous burst and an SLO breach probability curve. I’ll attach the sizing worksheet (redwood_sizing_worksheet.xlsx) in the next message for your internal ops to review.

Karthik

Tom — thanks for the CSV and the answers. Quick notes inline (pasted from Karthik’s sizing run):

> For the streaming fraction, is streaming used for first-token latency...

Karthik: client consumes tokens continuously for interactive sessions (web): streaming continues until end; server-side non-streaming for batch API.

Sizing summary (high level):
- Conservative pilot recommendation (14-day): 4 x A10G-equivalent GPUs (node isolation for KV cache), configured with 2x burst headroom slots (supports p95 < 400ms for baseline & p95 ~620ms during 3.4x burst).
- Aggressive production commit (90-day): 18 x A10G-equivalent GPUs across 3 racks; autoscale buffer + 1.5x reserved burst policy (estimated monthly reserved cost attached).

Deliverables we’ll send by EOD: final worksheet with node-by-node token throughput, expected p95 under traffic spike simulation, and a short MOP runbook for pilot. Olga has attached the worksheet to this thread.

Attachments: redwood_sizing_worksheet.xlsx

Next step: confirm one of Marissa’s slots — Tue Sep 2 14:00 PST works for our infra team. If procurement needs the draft vendor terms before the call, Marissa will share that doc.

Thanks — Hannah
